# APIs and services

## Scope

Applies when the change touches HTTP, gRPC, events, webhooks. Not when the interface stays inside one process, such as an internal function signature. Neighbours: `aidd-team:api-design`, `aidd-team:product-defaults`, `aidd-team:performance`.

## Standards

| # | Standard | Edition | Checked | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| S1 | OpenAPI Specification | 3.2.1 | 2026-09-29 | <https://spec.openapis.org/oas/v3.2.1.html> |

### Open choices

The team decides these. aidd's default holds until a `[[standards]]` entry fills one (`aidd standard list`).

| Choice | Question | aidd's default | Options |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `api-framework` | Which framework serves the API? | The framework the service already uses. For a new service, the ecosystem's common framework that serves the OpenAPI contract. | FastAPI, Hono, NestJS, ASP.NET Core minimal APIs, Spring Boot, axum, Go net/http |
| `validation-library` | Which library validates input against the contract at the boundary? | A schema library that the contract and the types come from, so one definition checks the input and documents it. | Pydantic, Zod, Valibot, JSON Schema with a validator, the framework's own validation |

## Checklist by loop step

| Step | Item | Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Entry (`aidd assess`) | A changed request, response, status code, event, GraphQL type, or Protobuf message is a contract change: never minor. | S1, S6 |
| Entry (`aidd assess`) | Product defaults (`api_conventions`, `data_conventions`, `operability`): build each one `[project.defaults] off` does not name, as `aidd-team:product-defaults` says. | — |
| Specify | The OpenAPI or AsyncAPI change, the GraphQL schema, or the `.proto` file is written before Spec approval and listed in `design.files`, so Spec approval freezes it. The Acceptance references its operations and schemas. | S1, S6 |
| Specify | Errors follow RFC 9457 problem details; every write has an idempotency strategy; rate limits, quotas, and spending limits on paid providers are stated (OWASP API4). | S2, S3, S4 |
| Implement | Validate input against the contract at the boundary. Authorize per object and per property (OWASP API1, API3). Paginate every list. A GraphQL server caps depth and cost and takes only persisted operations from first-party clients. | S3, S6 |
| Implement | Webhooks are signed and carry an id and a timestamp; a receiver verifies them and drops a replay (Standard Webhooks). | S8 |
| Review | Only additive changes without a version bump; removals go through expand and contract, announced by `Deprecation` and, once dated, `Sunset`. | S5, S7 |
| Ship | Consumer contract tests pass for every known consumer before rollout. 4xx and 5xx rates and p95 latency are the observe signals; calls to deprecated operations are counted per consumer. | S1, S7 |

## Test commands

| Command | Proves | How | Standard |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Spectral | the OpenAPI or AsyncAPI document lints clean against the team ruleset | `npx @stoplight/spectral-cli@6.16.3 lint openapi.yaml` in the test commands | S1 |
| Contract tests | every known consumer still passes against the head | consumer-driven, with Pact: each consumer's tests write its pact, and the provider verifies every consumer's pact against the head. The verification runs as a `[[tests.commands]]` entry (`command = ["npm", "run", "test:pact:verify"]`, or the stack's Pact verifier) with `when_changed` on the API code and its contract. At release: `pact-broker can-i-deploy --pacticipant <provider> --version <sha> --to-environment production` (pact_broker-client v1.78.0) | S1 |
| Schema conformance | the running API matches its contract | `uvx schemathesis==4.28.0 run <openapi-url>` against the running service | S1 |
| Breaking-change diff | no breaking change without a major version | `oasdiff breaking --fail-on ERR base.yaml openapi.yaml` (oasdiff v1.32.1), where a small script writes `base.yaml` from the base commit (`git show <base>:openapi.yaml`) first, as a `[[tests.commands]]` entry with `when_changed = ["openapi.yaml"]`; a breaking change passes only with a major version | S5 |
| GraphQL schema diff | no breaking GraphQL change without a major version, and every dangerous one named | `npx -p @graphql-inspector/cli@7.0.0 graphql-inspector diff base.graphql schema.graphql`, with `base.graphql` written from the base commit, as a `[[tests.commands]]` entry with `when_changed` on the schema | S6, S5 |
| Protobuf lint and breaking check | the `.proto` files lint clean and break no wire or JSON compatibility | `buf lint` and `buf breaking --against '.git#branch=main'` (buf v1.73.0), with `when_changed` on the `.proto` files | S5 |
| OWASP ZAP API scan | no high finding on the changed operations | `zap-api-scan.py` from the ZAP 2.17.0 image against a test deployment | S3 |
| Load test | the SLO holds under expected load | `k6 run` (k6 v2.3.0) with thresholds | — |

- From `aidd-team:product-defaults`: API conventions, Operability smoke.

## Keep it current

Each entry is due after its `review_every_days` (else emerging 90 days, established 365) or by its `review_due`. An emerging one applies only when the change needs it, said in the Spec. One `aidd eval standards` lists as due is looked up in Specify, and a missing one is proposed to aidd's `schemas/roles.json`. Steward: @thaithienvanid, who reviews every change to this pack's standards.
